title: Shared Ancestry in a Sorted Family Tree
description: Genealogists are analyzing a family tree represented as a Binary Search Tree (BST), where each person's identifier follows standard BST ordering rules. Given the root of the BST and two specific family members (nodes p and q), find their lowest common ancestor (LCA). The LCA is defined as the lowest node in the tree that has both p and q as descendants (where a node can be a descendant of itself).
constraints: p and q are existent in the BST.
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5].
input_format: Root of a BST, and two node values p and q.
output_format: The node representing the lowest common ancestor.

examples.explanation: The lowest common ancestor of 2 and 8 is 6.
A node can be a descendant of itself, so 2 is the LCA.
The root 2 is the ancestor for both itself and 1.
